newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul calls for "extraordinary alertness" on North.
newsitem.headline: Seoul calls for "extraordinary alertness" on North.

text.p: South Korean Prime Minister Lee Soo-sung on Tuesday called for "extraordinary alertness" against the North, saying a top Pyongyang official's defection showed serious instability in the Stalinist North.

"The defection of secretary Hwang Jang-yop, who belongs to the core force of the North Korean leadership, vividly displays the shaking of the ideological foundation that has supported the North Korean system amid economic disasters," he said.
Lee told parliament that communist North Korea has increasingly deployed offensive forces near the border with the South, despite an economic crisis and chronic food shortages.

The premier said the shooting of a prominent defector near Seoul at the weekend after Hwang sought political asylum in Seoul's mission in Beijing reminded South Koreans of the importance of security in the country.
Hwang, a senior adviser to North Korean leader Kim Jong-il, is now marooned in the South Korean mission.
"I think what we need at this point of time...is extraordinary aleartness and realisation," Lee said.
